learningObjective: Compare JIT and AOT compilation on optimization opportunities, deployment characteristics, and cold-start behavior.
stem: Which statements correctly compare Just-in-Time (JIT) and Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: JIT and AOT are mutually exclusive: a compilation pipeline can be either JIT or AOT but not combine both.

JIT compilation can exploit runtime information (observed types, hot call sites, actual input shapes) to specialize code adaptively; AOT lacks this dynamic profile unless PGO or similar techniques feed profiles back before deployment.
AOT produces deployable artifacts with no compilation cost at runtime, avoiding warm-up latency; JIT amortizes compile time across program execution and thus has a warm-up phase.
JIT is inherently less optimized than AOT because it must be fast to compile; AOT compilers can spend arbitrary time on optimization.

explanation: A: JIT sees runtime information (observed types, hot paths); AOT lacks this unless profile-guided. B: AOT avoids runtime compilation and its warm-up latency; JIT has a warm-up phase. C is wrong: JITs (V8, HotSpot) can spend significant compile budget on hot code, and can specialize adaptively; JITs are not inherently less optimized. D is wrong: modern systems mix both — HotSpot has AOT tiers (AppCDS, native-image), PyTorch has torch.compile (JIT) alongside torch.export (AOT), and V8's Sparkplug/TurboFan use tiered JIT with AOT-ish caches.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: modern systems mix JIT and AOT tiers.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: JIT's key advantage is runtime information; AOT lacks it without PGO.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: AOT has no runtime compile cost; JIT has warm-up.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: JITs can and do apply expensive optimizations to hot code; they are not inherently less optimized.

assumptions: Standard definitions of JIT and AOT in modern language runtimes and ML frameworks.
nonImplications: Does not imply JIT is always slower for cold-start; simple JITs can outperform AOT with poor profile.
Does not imply AOT always produces the same code as JIT; AOT lacks runtime specialization opportunities.

distractorRationales.A: Falsely treats JIT and AOT as mutually exclusive.
